summaries.body:
The 5.0 mapping records V16.4.1 as moved from 4.0.3 V7.3.1, whose text already required logging components to encode data to prevent log injection. Git agrees with the mapping. Abhay's 10 February 2019 CWE pass records V7.3.1; Andrew van der Stock updated V7 CWE items on 20 February 2019; Josh Grossman marked C9 on 24 February 2019.

On 21 February 2019 Andrew van der Stock filed #502: if 7.3.3 (log protection) is a prerequisite of 7.3.1 (log encoding), then encoding should be L2 because it sits behind the scenes and is not easily reached in most penetration tests. Commit 206e6700 the same day reordered 7.3.3 and 7.3.1 and moved 7.3.1 to L2. tghosth's 6 January 2019 "Specify proven crty" stamp on V7.3.1 is cryptography-chapter noise on this ID.

The 5.0 text is the same log-injection encoding requirement, minus the Proactive Control C9 marker. The material 4.0-era change attested here is the L2 promotion and reorder with 7.3.3 (#502). Elar Lang's 14 March 2021 commit 7c673d76 closed #887 (not in the issues list as a discussion of this wording). Cookie-prefix and SSRF events in the timeline are slot reuse.

decisions.statement: Log encoding (then V7.3.1) was made L2 because it sits behind log-protection and is not easily reached in most penetration tests.

key_sources.role: reordered log protection vs encoding and set encoding to L2
